# Scalar text verifier profile

This separate diagnostic job samples one normal `scalar_text` native search on Linux ARM64. It does not produce a native prerequisite or satisfy the required Native ARM64 host-tests aggregate. Its separately named artifact cannot be consumed as native acceptance evidence.

The harness constructs the same nineteen Oak/assembly/module inputs as the normal native prover and uses the full qualified package, supplied units, checked callee context, native compiler constructor, fresh-verdict mode and ordinary search. Only synthesized native function selection is restricted to the literal `scalar_text`. All three expected uncached candidate validations must complete in their normal order for comparison. An earlier proof, changed search order, extra/missing validation or resource refusal makes the diagnostic non-comparable; it never forces another validation or changes a proof allowance.

The dedicated `ubuntu-24.04-arm` job can add one ARM runner alongside the unchanged two-slot native matrix. It adds a visible diagnostic check; this source change does not change branch-protection settings. Its original thirty-minute deadline covers up to seven minutes for setup, nine for one race-enabled root harness build and its helper controls, eleven for one diagnostic, and three for final evidence, including a final one-minute upload reserve. Faster phases do not give a later phase a fresh whole-job allowance. The diagnostic itself reserves thirty seconds for source preparation, at most six hundred seconds for one `emitFor` call, and thirty seconds for profile finalization. Missing tools, empty/skipped controls, timeout, output overflow or incomplete finalization fail the diagnostic explicitly. There is no automatic retry.

CPU sampling uses Go 1.27.1's `runtime/pprof` default 100 Hz. Block sampling uses 1,000,000 ns and mutex sampling fraction 100. Rates are process-global in a fresh child. The coordinator stops CPU profiling; its asynchronous writer only reports a sticky error and never calls `StopCPUProfile` itself. Each profile has an 8 MiB writer cap. The three JSON files share 1 MiB, and combined command/compiler/timing output shares 2 MiB. The upload directory admits only the named profiles, exact nineteen sources, receipts, bounded parser summaries and owner metadata, at most 32 MiB. The binary, generated C and native object are not uploaded.

Checkout, official setup-go and the bounded privileged package-installation step run under the hosted workflow/VM supervisor inside the original setup allowance. The Python owner manages only unprivileged Go, harness and parser children; it does not claim to terminate root-owned package-manager descendants. The runner uses measured host/cgroup headroom and free disk for admission. Its proposed sampled cutoffs are 8 GiB process-tree RSS, 4 GiB logical owned build/cache/temp/binary data, and 2 GiB available-memory/free-disk reserves. Disk admission also reserves 64 MiB for raw and staged copies; only the staged copy is uploaded. Directory allocation and shared pages make logical bytes/RSS sums different from physical storage/memory. These observations are not hard isolation. The job does not set solver cgroups, address-space limits, GOGC, GOMEMLIMIT or GOMAXPROCS. Official setup-go and the Ubuntu host, loader and tool runtime remain trusted; hashes/version/build records bind the observed tool identities, not a complete independent proof of their distribution or loader closure.

A complete artifact requires the successful exact workflow command, zero child exit, pipe EOF, owned direct-child join, matching current checkout/input/harness identities, successful format parsing of all three profiles by the same Go toolchain, complete report validation and bounded staging. Accepted-looking result bytes alone are insufficient, because later close, reauthentication or staging can fail. On abnormal cutoff, compiler goroutines may still be active until the harness exits. The owner terminates the owned process group and waits for its direct child; it does not claim individual compiler-goroutine joining or arbitrary descendant reaping.

Interpretation stays narrow. Existing `bdd_joined` attribution includes admission, scheduling, cancellation, garbage collection, store release and joined coordinator wall time. CPU samples and block/mutex delays cannot be summed or subtracted to reconstruct that exclusive wall bucket. Sampling itself changes timing, allocation and order-race winners. This fresh process lacks the preceding functions' global admission/GC history. Three completed validations do not establish that their implication operands or selected couplings were identical, and a complete diagnostic is neither a speedup measurement nor full native-producer success.

The frozen input manifest is an intentional source-profile lock. Any solver/support source, candidate-name or toolchain change requires review of that lock and the diagnostic contract. The normal producer continues to reject an inherited `OAK_NATIVE_ONLY`; the diagnostic checks that refusal before installing its own fixed selector, and restores the original environment on return.

The diagnostic's process sampler refuses capped inventories, unreadable or malformed live PID/parent/state records and absent numeric RSS for a sampled live descendant. It permits only explicitly vanished process directories and zero-RSS zombies; unrelated kernel threads may lack RSS. This is a non-atomic parent-graph sample: process births, reparenting, exits and PID reuse between reads/samples can escape attribution. The existing required native telemetry helper remains unchanged. This stricter diagnostic can refuse a run on an observation race; it cannot silently accept incomplete metadata as a complete RSS sample.

Incoming CC, CXX or GOENV overrides are refused. Persistent Go environment files are disabled with GOENV=off; authenticated absolute C/C++ paths are supplied to Go, verified by its environment output, and the authenticated absolute Go executable is used for builds, test-event conversion and profile parsing. Tool hashes are checked again before acceptance. Repeated TERM/INT cancellation is deferred during the bounded group-signal/direct-wait cleanup sequence, then makes the diagnostic fail. Observation or signalling errors still lead to a direct-wait attempt; incomplete cleanup never grants success.

The fresh hosted race harness must pass all seven helper roots and 47 named children, with zero skips, before the profile can start. The Python owner requires its exact 29 methods. These checks do not claim that this profiling workload passed locally.
